findings.description: The start-up sequence treats a code 8 report as a detection, but permits status-high and task release only when no fault has been detected since reset. SWR-LAT-010 and SWR-LAT-011 require code 8 to leave start-up continuing unless the latch is set.
findings.requested_change: Distinguish a code 8 report from a fault that prevents normal start-up, including in the status-high and task-release conditions.

findings.description: The fault manager says every detection commands outputs low and inhibits both watchdogs, yet it also receives code 8. SWR-LAT-010 requires code 8 not to enter the safe state by itself, and CON-SUP-137 requires watchdog servicing to continue.
findings.requested_change: Specify a separate code 8 handling path that records and reports it without commanding the safe state or inhibiting watchdog service, except for the latch reaction at the third detection.

findings.description: The manager records history and increments the fault count on detection. SWR-SVC-007, SWR-SVC-009 and SWR-SVC-010 define these in terms of reports made; SWR-DIA-001 permits a fault interrupted by a watchdog reset to have no report.
findings.requested_change: Define when a report is made and update the retained report count and history consistently with that event, including interrupted fault handling.

findings.description: Compare events are armed exactly at the limit, but a measured value equal to the limit is within it. The item does not specify a later comparison if the task remains unstarted or executing, so a single event at equality can miss the violation required by SWR-TIM-001 and SWR-TIM-002.
findings.requested_change: Specify how the supervisor detects a continuing violation after equality within the 100 µs deadline, including event ordering at the limit.

findings.description: The scheduler releases the three 10 ms tasks and T_DIAG in a fixed pattern, although SWR-CFG-007 requires the task set, periods and release order to come from configuration so they can change without changing supervisor code.
findings.requested_change: Define scheduling in terms of the validated configuration, with the stated four-task schedule as the default rather than a fixed algorithm.

findings.description: The highest-priority task below the timer handler releases application tasks and then performs the end-of-cycle checkpoint check in the same sequence. It specifies no wait or scheduling point that lets those tasks execute and report checkpoints before the check.
findings.requested_change: Specify the execution contexts and ordering that allow the released tasks to run and submit their checkpoints before the end-of-cycle check, including the 100 ms task.

findings.description: The start-up task runs alone before other tasks start, yet SWC-SUP-011 transmits the RST and code 8 messages in the diagnostic task. SWR-RST-002 and SWR-RST-003 require those transmissions within 10 ms of reset classification, including while start-up checks are running.
findings.requested_change: Define how diagnostic transmission executes during start-up and meets both message deadlines and their required order.

findings.description: The status-high request checks fault state and then writes the pin, while the interrupt-context fault manager can command the pins low. Atomic individual pin writes do not prevent an interrupt between the check and the high write, which can leave the status high after a fault.
findings.requested_change: Specify synchronization or an equivalent ordering mechanism that prevents a status-high write after fault detection or latch setting.

findings.description: The inhibit flag can be set from interrupt context while a task services a watchdog. Atomic access to the flag alone does not prevent a fault interrupt between checking the flag and issuing a refresh, contrary to SWR-WDG-001.
findings.requested_change: Define synchronization or hardware-supported ordering that prevents a watchdog service after fault detection, including an interrupt during a service call.

findings.description: Invalid retained content is treated as power-on state. On a software or watchdog reset this can clear the latch, detection counts and history, conflicting with SWR-LAT-007, SWR-LAT-013 and SWR-LAT-014.
findings.requested_change: Distinguish confirmed power-on reset from invalid retained content after other resets, and specify a reaction that preserves the required retention behavior.

findings.description: On a full report queue the interface says the new report is queued after a bounded retry, but gives no storage for it while the queue remains full. The capacity covers only one cycle of reports, while SWR-DIA-001 requires each applicable report within 10 ms.
findings.requested_change: Define bounded admission, pending storage and transmission behavior for simultaneous or successive reports, and show how the required deadlines are met.

findings.description: The item states that each pin write is atomic and that pins are inputs from any reset, but cites software requirements and no controlled hardware reference supporting those hardware properties. CON-SUP-002 identifies RM0486 without a section or page.
findings.requested_change: Cite the controlled hardware reference for the claimed access and reset properties, or record the unsupported properties as open points.
